questions.stem: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance $L = 10\text{ mH}$, capacitance $C = 1\ \mu\text{F}$, and resistance $R = 100\ \Omega$. What is the quality factor ($Q$-factor) of this resonant circuit?
questions.shortSolution: Resonant angular frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-2} \times 10^{-6}}} = 10^4\text{ rad/s}$. The Q-factor is $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{10^4 \times 10^{-2}}{100} = 1$.

questions.stem: A wire of initial length $2\text{ m}$ and cross-sectional area $1\text{ mm}^2$ is stretched by a force of $100\text{ N}$. If Young's modulus of the wire is $2 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, find the elastic potential energy stored in the wire in millijoules (mJ).
questions.shortSolution: Elastic potential energy $U = \frac{1}{2} \frac{F^2 L}{A Y} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{100^2 \times 2}{10^{-6} \times 2 \times 10^{11}} = 0.05\text{ J} = 50\text{ mJ}$.

questions.stem: A moving coil galvanometer has a resistance of $50\ \Omega$ and yields full-scale deflection for a current of $2\text{ mA}$. The series resistance required to convert it into a voltmeter reading up to $10\text{ V}$ is:
questions.shortSolution: Using $V = I_g(R_g + R) \implies 10 = 2 \times 10^{-3} (50 + R) \implies 5000 = 50 + R \implies R = 4950\ \Omega$.

questions.stem: Two spherical raindrops with radii in the ratio $1 : 2$ fall vertically through air. Assuming laminar viscous drag, the ratio of their terminal velocities $v_1 / v_2$ is:
questions.shortSolution: Terminal velocity $v_t = \frac{2 r^2 (\rho - \sigma) g}{9 \eta} \propto r^2$. Therefore, $v_1 / v_2 = (r_1 / r_2)^2 = (1 / 2)^2 = 1 / 4$.

questions.stem: A uniform solid sphere of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.5\text{ m}$ rotates about a fixed axis passing through its center of mass with an angular velocity of $10\text{ rad/s}$. Calculate its angular momentum in $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}$.
questions.shortSolution: Moment of inertia $I = \frac{2}{5} M R^2 = \frac{2}{5} \times 2 \times (0.5)^2 = 0.2\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$. Angular momentum $L = I \omega = 0.2 \times 10 = 2\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}$.

questions.stem: As the temperature of a metallic conductor increases, its electrical resistance increases primarily because:
options: the relaxation time of free electrons decreases
the density of free electrons decreases
the relaxation time of free electrons increases
questions.answer: the relaxation time of free electrons decreases
questions.shortSolution: Resistivity $\rho = \frac{m}{n e^2 \tau}$. Higher temperature increases thermal vibrations, causing more frequent collisions, which decreases the average relaxation time $\tau$ and increases resistance.

questions.stem: Which of the following organic compounds will NOT undergo a Cannizzaro reaction when treated with concentrated sodium hydroxide solution?
questions.shortSolution: Cannizzaro reaction is given by aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens. Acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) contains $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes aldol condensation instead.

questions.stem: For the galvanic cell reaction $\text{Zn}(s) + \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu}(s)$, the standard cell potential $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V}$. What is the magnitude of standard Gibbs energy change $\Delta G^\circ$ in $\text{kJ/mol}$? (Use $F = 96500\text{ C/mol}$ and round to the nearest integer).
questions.shortSolution: $\Delta G^\circ = -n F E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -2 \times 96500 \times 1.10 = -212300\text{ J/mol} = -212.3\text{ kJ/mol}$. Magnitude is approximately $212\text{ kJ/mol}$.

questions.stem: Which of the following thermodynamic parameters is classified as an extensive property?
questions.shortSolution: Extensive properties depend on the mass/quantity of matter in the system. Enthalpy is extensive, whereas temperature, pressure, and molar heat capacity are intensive.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of a $10^{-3}\text{ M}$ aqueous solution of a fully dissociated monobasic strong acid at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.shortSolution: Since the acid is monobasic and fully dissociated, $[\text{H}^+] = 10^{-3}\text{ M}$. $\text{pH} = -\log_{10}[\text{H}^+] = -\log_{10}(10^{-3}) = 3$.

questions.stem: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ to yield salicylaldehyde, the active electrophile is:
questions.shortSolution: Chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) reacts with hydroxide ion to generate dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$), a neutral electron-deficient species acting as the electrophile.

questions.stem: In Lassaigne's test for qualitative detection of nitrogen in an organic compound, the characteristic Prussian blue complex formed is:
questions.shortSolution: Sodium cyanide formed during fusion reacts with $\text{FeSO}_4$ and ferric ions to form iron(III) hexacyanoferrate(II), $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3$, which gives the Prussian blue color.
